title: The Black Death
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point combines the 1347 arrival and the one-third death toll, which the arrival card covers, with the labour-shortage bargaining power, which the effects card covers, but neither card teaches both, and the effects card is broader, covering feudalism and the Peasants' Revolt.

draft.title: The Black Death
card: The Black Death was a plague that reached Europe in 1347. It spread quickly through towns and villages, carried by fleas on rats and by people.
It killed about a third of the people of Europe. Whole villages were left empty and many fields went unworked.
With so many dead, there were far fewer workers. This was a labour shortage, and landlords needed peasants to farm their land.
Surviving peasants could ask for better pay and conditions. Some landlords gave in, because they could not find other workers.
draft.remember: Many died, workers became scarce, and surviving peasants gained power to demand better pay.

a.q: After the Black Death, why could many surviving peasants ask for higher pay?
opts: Workers were scarce, so landlords needed them
Landlords had grown richer from the plague
The king ordered all wages to be raised
Fewer crops were needed, so work was easier
a.why: So many people died that there were few workers left, so landlords needed the survivors and had to offer more. The king did not order the rise, and the shortage was the reason peasants had power.
a.clue: Think about what happens when there are fewer workers than jobs.

b.q: In 1350, a landlord in a village that lost many people cannot find workers for his fields. What is he most likely to do?
opts: Offer better pay to keep the workers he has
Cut the pay of the workers who remain
Wait for the plague to return and end
Sell his land to the peasants for nothing
b.why: With few workers left, the landlord had to compete for them, so offering better pay was likely. Cutting pay would risk losing the few workers he had, since peasants could go elsewhere.
b.clue: He needs workers and there are few of them.

a.best: Workers were scarce, so landlords needed them

b.best: Offer better pay to keep the workers he has

problems.detail: Why (a) says landlords 'had to offer more', and why (b) says the landlord 'had to compete'. The card says only that 'some landlords gave in'. Many landlords, and the English Ordinance of Labourers of 1349, tried to hold wages down, so 'had to' overstates what the card teaches.

check.summary: Facts and answers are sound. The only issue is that the explanations say landlords 'had to' raise pay, while the card says only that some landlords gave in.

a.why: So many people died that few workers were left, so landlords needed the survivors, and some offered more to keep them. The king did not order a rise: it was the shortage of workers that gave peasants their power.
a.clue: Think about what happens when there are fewer workers than jobs.

b.q: In 1350, a landlord in a village that lost many people cannot find workers for his fields. What is he most likely to do?
opts: Offer better pay to keep the workers he has
Cut the pay of the workers who remain
Wait for the plague to end and workers to return
Sell his land to the peasants for nothing
b.why: With few workers left, offering better pay was his most likely way to keep them, as some landlords did. Cutting pay would risk losing the workers he had, since peasants could leave for a landlord who paid more.
b.clue: He needs workers and there are few of them.
